mock_data.title: A Donor Shortage
mock_data.passage:
The death of Dr Christiaan Barnard, the famous transplant surgeon, has occurred at a time when many of his modern counterparts are facing difficulties. Many of the early problems, such as tissue rejection, have, to a great extent, now been solved, thanks to the introduction of new drugs. However, there remains a major problem. The people in need of transplant surgery far outnumber the available organs.

The shortage of organ donors has caused several doctors to call for urgent improvements to be made to the system by which organs are donated. Many countries, such as Britain, have huge waiting lists of people whose lives could be saved by being given a kidney, lung, heart, or liver transplant. Sadly, many of them die before they reach the top of those lists.

Under the present British scheme, people are asked to carry donor cards, and/or put their names on the national donor register. Thus, if they lose their lives suddenly, for example, in a traffic accident, they have given permission in advance of their deaths for their organs to be used. If they have not done so, surgeons are faced with the task of asking the distraught next-of-kin for permission to use the organs of the deceased. Of course, often the relatives are too upset even to think of such a thing until it is too late. Organ transplants have to take place quite soon after the death of the donor.

Dying and donating organs is not something most of us like to think about, and only about 14% of people have registered. Now, it has been suggested that, instead of the present register, there should be a register of people who wish to opt out of having their organs removed for transplant surgery.

Increasing the number of donors is made more difficult because it is such an emotive issue. Just recently, an article in the Journal of the American Medical Association showed that half of the families in the United States refused, when asked for permission to use the organs of their loved ones.
mock_data.passageB1:
The death of Dr. Christiaan Barnard, a famous doctor who did transplant surgery, happened at a time when many doctors are having problems. In the past, there were problems like the body rejecting the new organ. But now, new medicines have helped to solve this problem.

However, there is still a big problem. There are many more people who need organ transplants than there are organs available. This shortage of organs is a serious issue.

Because of the lack of organ donors, some doctors say we need to improve the system for organ donation. Many countries, like Britain, have long waiting lists of people who need a new kidney, lung, heart, or liver. These transplants could save their lives. Sadly, many people die before it is their turn on the list.

In Britain, people can carry donor cards to show they want to donate their organs. They can also put their names on a national register. This means that if they die suddenly, like in a car accident, they have already given permission for their organs to be used. If they haven't done this, doctors must ask their family for permission. This is very difficult because the family is usually very upset and cannot think about it. Organ transplants must happen quickly after someone dies.

Most people don't want to think about dying and donating organs. Only a small number of people, about 14%, have signed up to be donors. Now, some people suggest that instead of a register for people who want to donate, there should be a register for people who don't want to donate their organs.

It is difficult to get more donors because it is a very emotional topic. Recently, a study showed that in the United States, half of the families asked for permission to use their loved one's organs said no. This makes it even harder to increase the number of organ donors.
mock_data.passageB2:
The recent death of Dr. Christiaan Barnard, a pioneer in transplant surgery, highlights the ongoing challenges faced by surgeons in this field. While significant strides have been made in overcoming issues like organ rejection, largely due to advancements in immunosuppressant drugs, a critical problem persists: the severe shortage of available organs for transplantation.

This acute lack of donors has led to calls for urgent improvements in organ donation systems. Countries like the UK have extensive waiting lists of patients whose lives could be dramatically improved, or even saved, through kidney, lung, heart, or liver transplants. Tragically, many of these individuals succumb to their illnesses before they can receive a life-saving organ.

Currently, the British system relies on individuals carrying donor cards and/or registering on a national donor database, indicating their consent for organ donation in the event of their death, for example, following a fatal accident. If a person hasn't registered, surgeons must ask the grieving family for permission to use the deceased's organs. Understandably, relatives are often too distraught to consider such a request, especially given the limited timeframe for successful organ transplantation. Organs need to be viable to transplant.

The difficulty is that death and organ donation are subjects most people avoid thinking about, resulting in a low registration rate – only around 14%. One proposed solution is to shift to an "opt-out" system, where individuals are automatically considered donors unless they explicitly register their refusal. This approach aims to address the current donor shortage by making donation the default option.

Increasing the number of donors remains a complex challenge due to the sensitive nature of the topic. A recent study in the Journal of the American Medical Association revealed that in the United States, approximately half of families decline permission when asked about donating a loved one's organs, highlighting the deep-seated emotional and ethical considerations surrounding this issue. It is a very delicate matter.
mock_data.passageC1:
The recent passing of Dr. Christiaan Barnard, a pioneering figure in transplant surgery, serves as a stark reminder of the enduring challenges facing his successors. While significant strides have been made in mitigating the early obstacles, most notably tissue rejection thanks to advancements in immunosuppressant drugs, a critical impediment persists: the acute disparity between the burgeoning demand for organ transplants and the patently insufficient supply of viable organs.

This chronic shortage has prompted a chorus of voices within the medical community to advocate for urgent and systemic reform of organ donation protocols. Across numerous nations, the United Kingdom being a prime example, protracted waiting lists are replete with individuals whose lives hang in the balance, contingent upon receiving a kidney, lung, heart, or liver transplant. Tragically, a significant proportion of these patients succumb to their illnesses before their turn arrives.

The existing British system relies on voluntary registration, whereby individuals are encouraged to carry donor cards and/or enlist in the national donor register. The intention is that, in the event of sudden death, such as from a traffic accident, prior consent will have been granted for organ retrieval. Absent such registration, surgeons are confronted with the delicate and often emotionally fraught task of soliciting consent from the bereaved next-of-kin. Understandably, relatives are frequently too overwhelmed to contemplate such a request, particularly given the time-sensitive nature of organ transplantation. Indeed, the window of opportunity for successful transplantation closes rapidly post-mortem.

The inherent morbidity associated with death and organ donation makes it a subject most individuals prefer to avoid, a fact reflected in the relatively low registration rate of approximately 14%. Consequently, a paradigm shift has been proposed, advocating for an opt-out system rather than the current opt-in model. This would entail establishing a register of individuals who actively object to organ donation, with the presumption that all others consent.

Heightening the donor pool is further complicated by the inherently emotive nature of the issue. A recent publication in the Journal of the American Medical Association highlighted that nearly half of families in the United States, when approached for consent, refused to authorize the use of their deceased loved ones' organs. This serves to underscore the deeply personal and often culturally contingent factors that underpin decisions regarding organ donation, and the significant challenge of overcoming public reticence.

mock_data.translation:
Mashhur transplantatsiya jarroh doktor Christiaan Barnardning o'limi uning zamonaviy hamkasblari qiyinchiliklarga duch kelayotgan bir paytda yuz berdi. To'qima rad etish kabi dastlabki muammolarning ko'pchiligi, yangi dorilarning joriy etilishi tufayili, katta darajada hal qilindi. Biroq, asosiy muammo saqlanib qolmoqda. Transplantatsiya jarrohligiga muhtoj odamlar soni mavjud organlardan ancha ko'p.

Organ donorlarining tanqisligi bir necha shifokorlarni organlar topshiriladigan tizimga shoshilinch yaxshilanishlar kiritishga chaqirdi. Buyuk Britaniya kabi ko'plab mamlakatlarda buyrak, o'pka, yurak yoki jigar transplantatsiyasi orqali hayotlarini saqlab qolish mumkin bo'lgan odamlarning ulkan kutish ro'yxatlari mavjud. Afsuski, ularning ko'pchiligi bu ro'yxatlarning boshiga yetib borishdan oldin vafot etadi.

Hozirgi Britaniya tizimida odamlardan donor kartalarini olib yurishlari va/yoki o'z nomlarini milliy donor reestrida qayd ettirishlari so'raladi. Shunday qilib, agar ular to'satdan, masalan, yo'l-transport hodisasida hayotdan ketsalar, ular o'limidan oldin organlaridan foydalanishga ruxsat berishgan bo'lishadi. Agar ular buni qilmagan bo'lsalar, jarrohlarga marhum organlaridan foydalanish uchun qayg'uli yaqin qarindoshlaridan ruxsat so'rash vazifasi yuklatiladi. Albatta, ko'pincha qarindoshlar juda xafa bo'lishadi va juda kech bo'lgunga qadar bu haqida o'ylashmaydi. Organ transplantatsiyasi donor o'limidan keyin juda tez amalga oshirilishi kerak.

O'lish va organlarni topshirish ko'pchiligimiz o'ylashni yoqtiradigan narsa emas va odamlarning atigi 14% ro'yxatdan o'tgan. Endi, hozirgi reestr o'rniga, transplantatsiya jarrohligida organlarini olib tashlashni xohlamaydigan odamlarning reestri bo'lishi kerakligi taklif qilindi.

Donorlar sonini oshirish qiyinroq, chunki bu juda emotsional masala. Yaqinda Amerika Tibbiy Assotsiatsiyasi jurnalida e'lon qilingan maqolada Qo'shma Shtatlardagi oilalarning yarmi o'z yaqinlarining organlaridan foydalanish uchun ruxsat so'ralganda rad etganligi ko'rsatildi.

mock_data.translationB1:
O‘tkazish jarrohligini amalga oshirgan mashhur shifokor, doktor Kristian Barnardning vafoti ko‘plab shifokorlar duch kelayotgan muammolar davriga to‘g‘ri keldi. Ilgari, tana yangi organni rad etishi kabi muammolar bo'lar edi. Ammo hozir yangi dorilar bu muammoni hal qilishga yordam berdi.

Biroq, hali ham katta muammo mavjud. Organ ko‘chirib o‘tkazishga muhtoj bo‘lganlar soni mavjud organlardan ancha ko‘p. Organlarning bu tanqisligi jiddiy masala hisoblanadi.

Organ donorlarining yetishmasligi sababli, ba'zi shifokorlar organ donorligi tizimini yaxshilashimiz kerakligini aytishmoqda. Britaniya kabi ko'plab mamlakatlarda yangi buyrak, o'pka, yurak yoki jigarga muhtoj bo'lgan odamlarning uzoq navbatlari mavjud. Bu ko'chirib o'tkazish jarrohliklari ularning hayotini saqlab qolishi mumkin edi. Afsuski, ko'pchilik navbatda o'z navbati kelishidan oldin vafot etadi.

Britaniyada odamlar o'z organlarini topshirishni xohlashlarini ko'rsatish uchun donor kartalarini olib yurishlari mumkin. Ular, shuningdek, o'z ismlarini milliy ro'yxatga kiritishlari mumkin. Bu shuni anglatadiki, agar ular to'satdan, masalan, avtohalokatda vafot etsalar, organlaridan foydalanish uchun allaqachon ruxsat bergan bo'lishadi. Agar ular buni qilmagan bo'lsalar, shifokorlar ularning oilasidan ruxsat so'rashlari kerak. Bu juda qiyin, chunki oila odatda juda xafa bo'ladi va bu haqda o'ylay olmaydi. Organ ko'chirib o'tkazish jarrohligi odam vafot etganidan keyin tezda amalga oshirilishi kerak.

Ko'pchilik o'lish va organ topshirish haqida o'ylashni xohlamaydi. Faqatgina oz sonli odamlar, taxminan 14% ro'yxatdan o'tgan. Endi, ba'zi odamlar organ topshirishni xohlovchilar uchun ro'yxat o'rniga, o'z organlarini topshirishni xohlamaydiganlar uchun ro'yxat bo'lishi kerakligini taklif qilishmoqda.

Ko'proq donorlarni topish qiyin, chunki bu juda hissiy mavzu. Yaqinda o'tkazilgan tadqiqot shuni ko'rsatdiki, Qo'shma Shtatlarda yaqinlarining organlaridan foydalanishga ruxsat so'ralgan oilalarning yarmi rad javobini bergan. Bu organ donorlari sonini ko'paytirishni yanada qiyinlashtiradi.
mock_data.translationB2:
Yaqinda transplantatsiya jarrohligida kashshof bo‘lgan doktor Kristian Barnardning vafoti bu sohada jarrohlar duch keladigan doimiy muammolarni yoritib beradi. Organ rad etilish kabi muammolarni yengib o‘tishda sezilarli qadamlar tashlangan bo‘lsa-da, asosan immunitetni bostiruvchi dorilarning rivojlanishi tufayli, hal qiluvchi muammo saqlanib qolmoqda: transplantatsiya uchun mavjud organlarning keskin yetishmasligi.

Donorlarning bu keskin yetishmasligi organ donorligi tizimini zudlik bilan yaxshilashga chaqiriqlarga sabab bo‘ldi. Buyuk Britaniya kabi mamlakatlarda buyrak, o‘pka, yurak yoki jigar transplantatsiyasi orqali hayoti keskin yaxshilanishi yoki hatto saqlab qolinishi mumkin bo‘lgan bemorlarning keng navbatlari mavjud. Afsuski, bu shaxslarning ko‘pchiligi hayotini saqlab qoluvchi organni olishdan oldin o‘z kasalliklariga taslim bo‘lishadi.

Hozirgi vaqtda Britaniya tizimi donorlik kartalariga ega bo‘lgan va/yoki milliy donorlar bazasida ro‘yxatdan o‘tgan shaxslarga tayanadi, bu ularning o‘limi holatida, masalan, halokatli baxtsiz hodisa natijasida organ donorligiga roziligini bildiradi. Agar shaxs ro‘yxatdan o‘tmagan bo‘lsa, jarrohlar marhumning organlaridan foydalanish uchun qayg‘uli oiladan ruxsat so‘rashlari kerak. Tushunarliki, qarindoshlar ko‘pincha bunday so‘rovni ko‘rib chiqishga juda qiynalishadi, ayniqsa organ transplantatsiyasi uchun cheklangan vaqtni hisobga olsak. Organlar transplantatsiya qilish uchun yaroqli bo'lishi kerak.

Qiyinchilik shundaki, o‘lim va organ donorligi mavzulari haqida ko‘pchilik o‘ylashdan qochadi, natijada ro‘yxatga olish darajasi past bo‘ladi – atigi 14% atrofida. Taklif qilingan yechimlardan biri "rad etish" tizimiga o‘tishdir, bunda shaxslar o‘z rad etishlarini aniq ro‘yxatdan o‘tkazmasa, avtomatik ravishda donor hisoblanadi. Bu yondashuv donorlikni odatiy variantga aylantirish orqali hozirgi donorlar yetishmasligini bartaraf etishga qaratilgan.

Donorlar sonini ko‘paytirish mavzuning nozikligi tufayli murakkab muammoligicha qolmoqda. Amerika Tibbiyot Assotsiatsiyasi jurnalida chop etilgan yaqinda o‘tkazilgan tadqiqot shuni ko‘rsatdiki, Qo‘shma Shtatlarda oilalarning taxminan yarmi yaqinlarining organlarini topshirish haqida so‘ralganda ruxsat berishdan bosh tortadi, bu esa ushbu masala atrofidagi chuqur ildiz otgan hissiy va axloqiy mulohazalarni ta’kidlaydi. Bu juda nozik masala.

Yaqinda transplantatsiya jarrohligida kashshof shaxs boʻlgan doktor Kristian Barnardning vafoti uning vorislari duch kelayotgan doimiy muammolarni keskin eslatib turadi. Dastlabki toʻsiqlarni, ayniqsa, immunosupressant dorilar yordamida toʻqimalarning rad etilishini yumshatishda sezilarli yutuqlarga erishilgan boʻlsa-da, muhim bir toʻsiq saqlanib qolmoqda: organ transplantatsiyasiga boʻlgan ortib borayotgan talab va yaroqli organlarning yetarli emasligi oʻrtasidagi oʻtkir nomutanosiblik.

Ushbu surunkali yetishmovchilik tibbiyot hamjamiyatida organ donorligi protokollarini zudlik bilan va tizimli ravishda isloh qilishni yoqlab chiqqan ovozlarning xoriga sabab boʻldi. Koʻplab davlatlarda, Buyuk Britaniya bunga yaqqol misol boʻla oladi, uzoq navbatlar buyrak, oʻpka, yurak yoki jigar transplantatsiyasini olishga bogʻliq boʻlgan, hayoti qil ustida turgan odamlarga toʻla. Afsuski, bu bemorlarning katta qismi oʻz navbati kelishidan oldin kasallikdan vafot etadi.

Mavjud Britaniya tizimi koʻngilli roʻyxatga olishga asoslanadi, bunda odamlar donorlik kartalarini olib yurishga va/yoki milliy donorlar roʻyxatiga kiritilishga undaladi. Maqsad shuki, toʻsatdan oʻlim holatida, masalan, yoʻl-transport hodisasidan, organlarni olish uchun oldindan rozilik berilgan boʻladi. Bunday roʻyxatga olish boʻlmagan taqdirda, jarrohlar qaygʻuli qarindoshlardan rozilik soʻrashning nozik va koʻpincha hissiy jihatdan murakkab vazifasiga duch kelishadi. Tushunarliki, qarindoshlar koʻpincha bunday soʻrov haqida oʻylashga juda charchagan boʻladilar, ayniqsa organ transplantatsiyasining vaqtga bogʻliqligini hisobga olsak. Haqiqatan ham, muvaffaqiyatli transplantatsiya uchun imkoniyat oynasi oʻlimdan keyin tezda yopiladi.

Oʻlim va organ donorligi bilan bogʻliq boʻlgan xastalik koʻpchilik odamlarning qochishni afzal koʻradigan mavzuga aylantiradi, bu taxminan 14% ga yaqin boʻlgan nisbatan past roʻyxatga olish darajasida aks etadi. Shunday qilib, hozirgi kirish modelidan koʻra, chiqish tizimini yoqlab, paradigma oʻzgarishi taklif qilindi. Bu organ donorligiga faol ravishda qarshi boʻlgan shaxslarning roʻyxatini tuzishni nazarda tutadi, qolganlarning barchasi rozilik bergan deb taxmin qilinadi.

Donorlar havzasini kengaytirish masalaning tabiatan hissiy ekanligi bilan yanada murakkablashadi. Amerika Tibbiyot Assotsiatsiyasi jurnalida yaqinda chop etilgan maqolada, Qoʻshma Shtatlardagi oilalarning deyarli yarmi rozilik soʻralganda, vafot etgan yaqinlarining organlaridan foydalanishga ruxsat berishdan bosh tortgani taʼkidlangan. Bu organ donorligi bilan bogʻliq qarorlarni asoslovchi chuqur shaxsiy va koʻpincha madaniy jihatlarga ishora qiladi va jamoatchilikning tortinchoqligini yengishning muhim muammosini koʻrsatadi.
